subject: cat-act-2011-lqa
note: 2A, 2026-10-01. Every cross-reference made by Parts 1-2 of the Cat Act 2011 (00-l0-01) and by the Cat Regulations 2012 provisions they depend on, plus the Interpretation Act and other meta-legislation they rely on without citing (marked 'Implicit'). All at depth 1: the regulation provisions are inside this run's scope, so references they make are first-step references. Module names are proposals; nothing is encoded yet (4A). References internal to Parts 1-2 (for example s. 9(3) to s. 14(2)) are not listed.

entries.to: Cat Act 2011 s. 37 (approval to breed cats; Part 3 Div. 4)
entries.reason: Parts 1-2 read only whether a person holds a current approval (ss. 18(2)(b), 23(2)(a)(ii)); the grant, refusal and duration rules in s. 37 and Cat Regs rr. 21-24 do not change any Part 2 outcome. Revisit at 4A if a finding turns on how an approval ends (s. 38, r. 24).

entries.to: police officer (Police Act 1892)
entries.reason: Who is a police officer is a status fact. Parts 1-2 never use 'authorised person'; the definition matters to Parts 3-4.

entries.to: Public Health Act 2016 s. 24(1) (designation as an authorised officer for the purposes of the Cat Act)
entries.reason: Whether a person has been so designated is a status fact; the term is not used in Parts 1-2.

entries.to: Local Government Act 1995 s. 9.10(2) (appointment of authorised persons)
entries.reason: Whether a person has been appointed is a status fact; the term is not used in Parts 1-2. Target is in the 0H reference set (wa-local-government-act-1995) if it is ever needed.

entries.to: Cat Regulations 2012 r. 4 (prescribed operators: Cat Haven, RSPCA WA)
entries.reason: In scope for this run (a regulation provision Parts 1-2 depend on), so encoded as part of the subject, not as a boundary module. Part 2 reaches the term through s. 3(1) transfer (b) and r. 9(2)(d).

entries.to: facilities operated by, or approved in writing by, a local government
entries.reason: Whether a facility is operated or approved by a local government is a fact; no provision governs the approval.

entries.to: Cat Regulations 2012 r. 5(1) (device must comply with AS 5018-2001 and AS 5019-2001)
entries.reason: In scope for this run (a regulation provision Parts 1-2 depend on), so encoded as part of the subject, not as a boundary module.

entries.to: Australian Standards AS 5018-2001 and AS 5019-2001 (Electronic Animal Identification), 'as amended from time to time'
entries.reason: Whether a device complies with the Standards is a technical fact. The Standards are Standards Australia's paid copyright and were not gathered.

entries.to: Cat Regulations 2012 r. 6 (four prescribed companies; (b) and (e) deleted)
entries.reason: In scope for this run (a regulation provision Parts 1-2 depend on), so encoded as part of the subject, not as a boundary module.

entries.to: Cat Regulations 2012 r. 7(1) (prescribed persons) and r. 7(2) (prescribed qualifications)
entries.reason: In scope for this run (a regulation provision Parts 1-2 depend on), so encoded as part of the subject, not as a boundary module.

entries.to: Veterinary Practice Act 2021 s. 3 (veterinary nurse: registered under Part 2)
entries.reason: Registration as a veterinary nurse is a status fact. VPA held in the bundle (veterinary-practice-act-2021).

entries.to: Vocational Education and Training Act 1996 s. 5(1) (registered training provider); the named units of competency and courses
entries.reason: Whether a person completed a named unit and course with a registered provider is a fact about that person.

entries.to: Cat Regulations 2012 r. 8 (implanted by a microchip implanter)
entries.reason: In scope for this run (a regulation provision Parts 1-2 depend on), so encoded as part of the subject, not as a boundary module.

entries.to: Veterinary Practice Act 2021 s. 3 (veterinarian: a WA veterinarian or an interstate veterinarian)
entries.reason: Registration status is a fact; nothing in Parts 1-2 turns on the VPA's registration rules. VPA held in the bundle.

entries.to: Cat Act 2011 Part 3 Div. 3 (reclaiming a cat from a cat management facility, ss. 32-34)
entries.reason: Part 2 needs only the event 'the cat was reclaimed from a facility'; the facility process is Part 3.

entries.to: Cat Act 2011 s. 76 (general regulation-making power) and the Cat Regulations 2012
entries.reason: Every 'prescribed' in Parts 1-2 resolves to a Cat Regulations 2012 provision listed separately below; s. 76 itself is the power, not encoded.

entries.to: Local Government Act 1995 s. 1.4 and Part 2 (terms used: local government, district; ss. 2.1, 2.5)
entries.reason: Parts 1-2 use 'local government' and 'district'; which local government a cat's place of keeping falls under is a geographic fact. The LGA is in the 0H reference set (wa-local-government-act-1995); no LGA definition used in Parts 1-2 changes an outcome. Revisit if a finding turns on another LGA-defined term.

entries.to: Cat Regulations 2012 r. 9 (cats exempt from registration: custody of named bodies, CMFs, veterinary premises; foster care)
entries.reason: In scope for this run (a regulation provision Parts 1-2 depend on), so encoded as part of the subject, not as a boundary module.

entries.to: Biosecurity Act 2015 (Cth): the Commonwealth Department administered by its Minister
entries.reason: Which Department has custody is a fact.

entries.to: Veterinary Practice Act 2021 s. 3 (veterinary premises: premises registered under Part 3)
entries.reason: Registration of premises is a status fact.

entries.to: Cat Regulations 2012 r. 10 (exemption while exhibited at a show of a named cat body)
entries.reason: In scope for this run (a regulation provision Parts 1-2 depend on), so encoded as part of the subject, not as a boundary module.

entries.to: Cat Regulations 2012 r. 11 and Schedule 1 Form 1 Parts A, B, D, F, G; Schedule 3 (fees)
entries.reason: In scope for this run (a regulation provision Parts 1-2 depend on), so encoded as part of the subject, not as a boundary module.

entries.to: 'such other requirements, if any, prescribed'
entries.reason: No regulation prescribes further requirements for s. 8(2)(c). Encoded in the regulations module as an explicit empty set, so it is a recorded decision and a later regulation cannot pass silently.

entries.to: Rates and Charges (Rebates and Deferments) Act 1992 s. 3(1) (eligible pensioner)
entries.reason: Pensioner status is a fact; it changes only the fee amount.

entries.to: offences against the Dog Act 1976 and the Animal Welfare Act 2002 (and against 'this Act', including Parts 3-6)
entries.reason: Only the number and dates of convictions matter; supplied as facts. Whether a conviction is spent (Spent Convictions Act 1988) was not considered at 2A.

entries.to: Oaths, Affidavits and Statutory Declarations Act 2005 (statutory declaration)
entries.reason: Whether information was verified by statutory declaration is a fact.

entries.to: Cat Regulations 2012 r. 12 (registration for 1 year, 3 years or life; expiry on 31 October; renewal within 21 days before 1 November)
entries.reason: In scope for this run (a regulation provision Parts 1-2 depend on), so encoded as part of the subject, not as a boundary module.

entries.to: Cat Regulations 2012 r. 14 and Form 2 (registration certificate)
entries.reason: In scope for this run (a regulation provision Parts 1-2 depend on), so encoded as part of the subject, not as a boundary module. Form content encoded only as the fields it requires.

entries.to: Cat Regulations 2012 r. 15 (registration tag: number, local government, colour by expiry year; lifetime tag orange)
entries.reason: In scope for this run (a regulation provision Parts 1-2 depend on), so encoded as part of the subject, not as a boundary module. Made under s. 76(2)(a), not cited by s. 11, but it defines what a registration tag must be.

entries.to: Minister's notice in the Gazette designating expiry-year colours
entries.reason: Which colour a year carries is a fact from a Gazette notice that was not searched for.

entries.to: Cat Regulations 2012 r. 16 (information recorded in the local government register)
entries.reason: In scope for this run (a regulation provision Parts 1-2 depend on), so encoded as part of the subject, not as a boundary module.

entries.to: Cat Act 2011 Part 4 Div. 5 (ss. 68-72: objection to the local government, review by the State Administrative Tribunal, suspension of decisions)
entries.reason: s. 13 needs only that the notice states the rights; the objection and review machinery is outside this run's scope (Parts 1-2). Note that s. 72 (registration continues pending objection or review) changes whether a cat is 'registered' for ss. 5-6; revisit at 4A if a finding turns on it.

entries.to: Cat Regulations 2012 r. 17 (information a microchip implanter gives the database company)
entries.reason: In scope for this run (a regulation provision Parts 1-2 depend on), so encoded as part of the subject, not as a boundary module. No form is prescribed under s. 15 ('form, if any, prescribed'): encoded as no form.

entries.to: Cat Act 2011 s. 15, and through it Cat Regulations 2012 r. 17
entries.reason: In scope for this run (a regulation provision Parts 1-2 depend on), so encoded as part of the subject, not as a boundary module.

entries.to: 'a class of cats prescribed as exempt from sterilisation'
entries.reason: No regulation prescribes a class for either provision (the Cat Regulations have no s. 18(2)(c) regulation). Encoded in the regulations module as an explicit empty class, so the empty set is a recorded decision and a later regulation cannot pass silently.

entries.to: Cat Regulations 2012 r. 18 (identified as sterilised by a s. 21 certificate or an ear tattoo)
entries.reason: In scope for this run (a regulation provision Parts 1-2 depend on), so encoded as part of the subject, not as a boundary module. The specimen tattoo is an image, in the docx only.

entries.to: 'in the form, if any, prescribed'
entries.reason: No form is prescribed for the s. 20 notice. Encoded in the regulations module as an explicit 'no form', so a later regulation cannot pass silently.

entries.to: Cat Regulations 2012 r. 19 (s. 23(1) and (2) do not apply to a transfer to an organisation or person in r. 9)
entries.reason: In scope for this run (a regulation provision Parts 1-2 depend on), so encoded as part of the subject, not as a boundary module.

entries.to: Interpretation Act 1984 s. 72 (a penalty at the foot of a section or subsection makes a contravention an offence)
entries.reason: Implicit: not cited by the text, applied by IA s. 3. Part 2 creates its offences only by 'Penalty:' lines, so the encoding needs s. 72 to know which contraventions are offences. IA is in the 0H reference set (wa-interpretation-act-1984).

entries.to: Interpretation Act 1984 s. 61 (computation of time; excluded days)
entries.reason: Implicit. Part 2 has 7-, 14- and 21-day periods; whether the start day counts and whether excluded days extend a deadline is set by s. 61. In the 0H reference set.

entries.to: Interpretation Act 1984 s. 71 (continuing offences: duty continues after the period; further offence each day after conviction, $50)
entries.reason: Implicit. Decides whether a late notice or a still-unregistered cat is one offence or many. In the 0H reference set.

entries.from: ss. 5(1), 14(1), 18(1) ('6 months of age') and r. 12
entries.to: Interpretation Act 1984 s. 62 (months, reckoning of)
entries.reason: Implicit. Fixes the day a cat 'has reached 6 months of age'. In the 0H reference set.

entries.to: Criminal Code (WA) Chapter V (ss. 22-36, criminal responsibility), applied by Code s. 36
entries.reason: Implicit. Meta-legislation joins the library only when a finding needs it (LQA-PIPELINE.md, The jurisdiction library). In the 0H reference set (wa-criminal-code). Relevant to the s. 6(3) defence if a finding turns on its relation to Code s. 23-24.

entries.to: Criminal Procedure Act 2004 (prosecution; s. 21 limitation) and Sentencing Act 1995 (applying a maximum fine)
entries.reason: Implicit; procedure and sentencing after an offence, not whether one is committed. Both in the 0H reference set. Prosecution and infringement notices for Part 2 offences are Part 4 (ss. 61-67, 73) and Cat Regs r. 30 and Sch. 2, also out of scope.

entries.to: Cat Act 2011 Part 4 Div. 4 (ss. 61-67) and Cat Regulations 2012 r. 30, Sch. 2 (modified penalty $200)
entries.reason: Not cited by Part 2: the infringement scheme cites Part 2. Listed so 3H sees the boundary. Out of scope for a Parts 1-2 run.

entries.to: Cat Act 2011 s. 88 (transitional: information in the centralised registration system taken to be recorded in a local government's register)
entries.reason: s. 88 is in Part 7 and is in force; it changes what counts as 'recorded in the register' under s. 12 before Stop Puppy Farming s. 59 commences. Supplied as a fact (whether information was recorded or transferred into the system); the encoding should say so.
